Article Title: Jharkhand student protest Day 14: Hunger strike continues as BJP, Rahul Gandhi back students
Article Text:
Students protest in Ranchi's Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium.

BJP MLAs protest outside Assembly

Rahul Gandhi speaks to aspirants

11-member delegation finalised

Officials reach protest site

'Assembly gherao' on Monday

NEW DELHI: The protest by JPSC and JSSC aspirants in Jharkhand entered its 14th day on Thursday, with students demanding action over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations, while political pressure on the Hemant Soren government intensified.The protest, launched on July 25 under the JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch at Ranchi's Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium, has grown into one of Jharkhand’s largest student-led movements in recent years. Protesters are seeking cancellation of the 14th JPSC Civil Services Preliminary Examination, an independent probe into alleged irregularities, and comprehensive reforms in the JPSC and JSSC. Here are the top developments:BJP MLAs on Thursday staged a protest outside the Jharkhand Assembly, on the first day of the Monsoon Session, over alleged irregularities in the state competitive examinations.Speaking to ANI, BJP MLA Alok Chaurasia said, "The Bharatiya Janata Party stands firmly and vocally with the students regarding the functioning of Jharkhand government agencies such as JPSC, JSSC, and CJL, as well as the widespread corruption across the state, particularly the fraud committed against students..."The legislators raised slogans against the government, with chief whip Naveen Jaiswal alleging it was "selling" Jharkhand's youths' future and demanding a CBI probe, saying, "nobody trusts your CID and committee." Rahul Gandhi speaks to aspirantsCongress leader Rahul Gandhi spoke to JPSC-JSSC aspirants over the phone on Thursday. Student leader Piyush Kumar said the students raised their demand for cancellation of the examination, an investigation and reforms."We told him of our demands, that exam should be cancelled, regarding investigation and reforms. He said that he stands with our demands, and that they will take it up with the Govt. He said that he stands with and supports students...We are yet to get any official information regarding the date and time of meeting (with the government)," Kumar said.Student leader Ravindra Paswan said Gandhi enquired about the situation at the protest site."He asked us about the situation here. We told him about the irregularities in exams here. We told him that Congress is in the government in Jharkhand and they should help us. He told us that he stands with students," Paswan said.According to JPSC JSSC Reform Manch, protesting students have finalised an 11-member delegation for talks with the state government. The group comprises eight student representatives, one lawyer and two technical experts.The eight student representatives are Piyush Kumar Singh, Ravindra Paswan, Rajesh Prasad, Neetu Kujur, Kartik Soren, Ravindra, Ankit Kumar and Shalu Singh.Students have also demanded that any dialogue with the government be held in the presence of the media.Ranchi Sadar SDO Rajat Kumar and ADM Dhananjay Kumar reached Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium to hear the grievances of the protesting aspirants."We came to speak with our younger brothers about how we can assist them in their preparations for the future," Rajat Kumar said.A protester said there had been a suggestion that a four- or five-member delegation should participate in talks, but students insisted on a transparent process.Amid the continuing agitation, students announced a "Vidhan Sabha Gherao" on August 10 if their demands are not met. Protester Radhe Kumar said the decision was taken after the government initiated contact with the students.JMM MLA Jairam Kumar Mahato urged the government to immediately open talks, warning that "something untoward will happen" if the situation remains unresolved.Activist Sonam Wangchuk rejected reports that student leader Devendra Nath Mahato had ended his hunger strike after speaking with him. A total of six demonstrators are presently on a hunger strike.In a video message on X, Wangchuk said, "He consumed water, not food; I want to clarify this."He added, "He was fasting without water and without food, which is, in a way, like suicide. So, I only urged him to consume water and salt now and continue his fast."Mahato began his indefinite hunger strike on August 2 at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium. He is now continuing the fast on water and salt.Jharkhand minister Shilpi Neha Tirkey said on Thursday that the government was investigating the allegations and that 19 people had been arrested.
Article Summary: Protest by jpsc and jssc aspirants in jharkhand entered its 14th day on thursday. Students demanding action over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations. Political pressure on the hemant soren government intensified. Protesters seeking cancellation of the 14th jpsc civil services preliminary examination, an independent probe into alleged irregularities.

Article Title: Rahul Gandhi flags Ken-Betwa tribal displacement; Centre forwards complaints to MP govt
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi raises Ken-Betwa displacement issue

NEW DELHI: The Union ministry of tribal affairs on Thursday told the Lok Sabha that it has received several representations raising concerns over the displacement of people due to the Ken-Betwa river-link project in Madhya Pradesh.The ministry said it has forwarded the representations to the state government and the concerned district administrations for examination and appropriate action.In a written reply to questions from Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi and Samajwadi Party MP Ajendra Singh Lodhi on the rehabilitation of tribal families affected by the project, compliance with the Forest Rights Act (FRA), and alleged evictions, the ministry said it had not received any complaints specifically claiming that compensation disbursed under the project had failed to reach beneficiaries.The ministry, however, said it had received representations "raising issues of displacement" due to the project.It added that the representations had been forwarded to the Madhya Pradesh government and the concerned district administrations for examination and appropriate action, while noting that the implementation of the Forest Rights Act (FRA) rests with state governments and Union Territory administrations.Minister of state for tribal affairs Durgadas Uikey, in his written reply, said the representations had been referred to the state authorities. "These have been forwarded to the State Government of Madhya Pradesh and respective District Administrations for examination and necessary action," the reply said.In its response, the ministry said the rehabilitation plan for Scheduled Tribe families affected by the Ken-Betwa river-link project was based on a proposal submitted by the National Water Development Agency in 2016.Citing the 2016 proposal, the ministry said the project's first phase is expected to displace 1,913 families comprising 8,339 people, including 648 Scheduled Tribe families.Responding to questions on gram sabha meetings under the Forest Rights Act (FRA), the ministry said it does not maintain centralised records of meeting dates, attendance, signatures, grievances related to consent, compensation and displacement, or the status of their disposal, as implementation of the law falls under the jurisdiction of state governments and Union Territory administrations.The ministry added that it has repeatedly urged states and UTs to ensure that no eligible beneficiary is denied forest rights and to strictly comply with Section 4(5) of the FRA, which prohibits the eviction or removal of claimants from forest land under their occupation until the process of recognition and verification of their rights has been completed.The Centre's response comes amid a prolonged protest by tribal families and other residents affected by the Ken-Betwa river-link project in Madhya Pradesh's Chhatarpur district over issues related to displacement, rehabilitation and resettlement.As part of the agitation, protesters staged a series of symbolic demonstrations in July, including a "jal satyagraha", "chita (pyre) satyagraha" and "faansi satyagraha".The protest also included an indefinite hunger strike by activist Amit Bhatnagar, who was later forcibly removed from the site by state police. Nearly 150 villagers were also removed during the operation, visuals of which drew nationwide attention.
Article Summary: Rahul gandhi raises ken-betwa displacement issue with lok sabha. Union ministry of tribal affairs says it has received several representations raising concerns over the displacement of people. The ministry said it has forwarded the representations to the state government and the concerned district administrations for examination.

Article Title: Temporary disability cert no bar for PwBD quota MBBS seat: NMC
Article Text:
Under the revised norms, candidates won't be denied admission merely because their UDID card or disability certificate is temporary.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Candidates cannot be denied admission to MBBS courses under the PwBD quota solely because they hold a temporary disability certificate or Unique Disability Identity (UDID) card, National Medical Commission (NMC) said. However, it made it clear that their disability status will continue to be verified by medical assessment boards (MABs) before they are declared eligible for counselling.In an addendum to "Guidelines on Assessment of Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD) for Admission to the MBBS Course, 2026", NMC Wednesday said the change has been made to ensure that the guidelines are interpreted in line with the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, 2024 Rules and a 2025 office memorandum issued by the department of empowerment of persons with disabilities.Under the revised norms, candidates whose disabilities are categorised as progressive, non-progressive or not likely to improve will not be denied admission merely because their UDID card or disability certificate is temporary. Their disability status, however, will continue to be verified by designated MABs before an eligibility certificate is issued. Candidates holding temporary UDID cards whose disability has been recorded as "likely to improve" will undergo reassessment before their eligibility is decided.MABs will also assess each candidate's functional competency."This year's revised guidelines unnecessarily created a new hurdle by introducing a distinction between temporary and permanent disabilities. I received multiple representations from students who were being harassed at assessment centres in Agartala, Mumbai and Delhi. That prompted us to submit a representation to NMC and raise this issue in the ongoing SC hearing as well," disability rights activist Prof Satendra Singh said.NMC said the addendum has been issued to ensure uniform implementation of admission guidelines and should be read as an integral part of the July 27 notification.
Article Summary: Under the revised norms, candidates won't be denied admission merely because their udid card or disability certificate is temporary. Nmc said the change has been made to ensure that the guidelines are interpreted in line with the rights of persons with disabilities act, 2016, 2024 rules and a 2025 office memorandum.

Article Title: Settling with a few cases won't stop CBI probe: Supreme Court warns realtors
Article Text:
SC said in court monitored investigations, sanctions for prosecution should be granted promptly

Many bank officials found to have colluded with realtors, Supreme Court told

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court has put a spoke in efforts of defaulting realtors to escape CBI probe by settling with a few homebuyers. The court said these builders would continue to be investigated for cheating homebuyers and siphoning off their deposits till the last of the flat purchasers get their property or refund.Many homebuyers had become parties to petitions filed by groups of homebuyers pleading similar cause – enormous delay in project completion by builders who have already received money through banks under subvention and the banks insisting on repayment in disregard of the fact that the flats are yet to be delivered.Advocate Pranav Sachdeva told a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that the court may allow those homebuyers, with whom defaulting builders has settled, to withdraw from petition and continue proceedings for the remaining homebuyers left high and dry by builders.Additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati, appearing for CBI, informed that the agency had completed probe in 18 of 50 cases in which CBI registered FIRs on SC’s orders. A total of 17 chargesheets and a closure report have been filed before competent courts.She said the chargesheets name several bank officials who were found to have colluded with builders. The agency has invoked provisions of the Prevention of Corruption Act against them and CBI has sought sanction to prosecute the officials from State Bank of India, Bank of India, Uco Bank, HDFC and ICICI.SC said in court monitored investigations, sanctions for prosecution should be granted promptly and directed these banks to give necessary permissions within two weeks for prosecution of the accused bank officials. “Failure to accord sanction within two weeks would require banks to submit explanations to the court,” it said and asked CBI to share documents on money trail to ED for initiation of inquiry under PMLA.On some complaints regarding alleged defaulting builders in other states, across states, the bench directed the CBI to conduct a thorough investigation into the allegations of misrepresentation and other irregularities by entities such as Ozone group in Karnataka, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu; Vivansaa in Bengaluru; Rudra Buildwell Pvt Ltd in Greater Noida, and Omaxe group in Chandigarh. A separate status report in respect of investigations into these builders and related banking institutions shall be submitted to the court.The main allegation, as crystallized by amicus Rajiv Jain, against these builders is that they don’t have ownership title over the land and have partnered leaseholders to construct housing projects. However, they advertised as if they owned the land, entered into agreements with homebuyers and financial institutions without the lessee being a part thereof and remained unaccountable for delay and default.Given the expanding workload, Bhati informed SC that CBI had sought additional hands from states for expediting the investigations but none of the states have responded to the CBI director’s request. The bench directed the DGPs of UP, TN, Karnataka, Maharashtra and Punjab to send on deputation required number of personnel, as requested by CBI, within 10 days.
Article Summary: Sc said in court monitored investigations, sanctions for prosecution should be granted promptly. Many bank officials found to have colluded with realtors, supreme court told. The court said these builders would continue to be investigated for cheating homebuyers and siphoning off their deposits.

Article Title: Udhayanidhi Stalin arrested from Chennai home over 'vulgar' remark against actor Trisha during rally
Article Text:
Udhayanidhi Stalin faced detention after a case was registered against him





CHENNAI: DMK leader and leader of opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin was arrested from his residence in Neelankarai on Tuesday after a case was registered against him over his allegedly objectionable remarks made during a rally on the Cauvery water dispute in Thanjavur.A police team led by Joint Commissioner of Police Dr P Vijayakumar took Udhayanidhi into custody from his residence and escorted him in a police vehicle. He will be taken to Thanjavur, where the FIR was registered in connection with his speech at Monday's rally on the Cauvery water dispute.Read More: 3,000 cops, one leader: Udhayanidhi decries 'terrorist'-style arrest by TVK govt The detention came after Udhayanidhi moved the Madras high court seeking anticipatory bail, apprehending arrest in the case. When the matter was mentioned before Justice G K Ilanthiraiyan, the court agreed to hear the urgent plea and orally directed the police not to precipitate the issue until the petition was taken up.Speaking to reporters after being detained, Udhayanidhi dismissed the case as "forged" and said he would fight it legally. He alleged that since the TVK government came to power, it had been filing "fake cases" against DMK MLAs and indulging in "horse-trading."During the rally, sections of the crowd began chanting "Trisha, Trisha". After pausing briefly, Udhayanidhi allegedly remarked, "Whether the water reaches anywhere else or not, it should reach there," before adding that he was referring to the Cauvery water.The controversy erupted after the remarks, with opposition parties accusing the DMK leader of making a double-entendre comment targeting Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay while responding to slogans raised by party workers.Based on a complaint filed by Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), Thanjavur police registered an FIR against Udhayanidhi under charges of promoting enmity between groups, provisions of the Information Technology Act, and the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Women Act.TVK also approached the National Commission for Women (NCW), alleging that Udhayanidhi's remarks were "vulgar", "objectifying" and "sexually suggestive". In its complaint, the party sought legal action against the DMK leader, an unconditional public apology and intervention by the commission.TVK national spokesperson Pazha Selvakumar alleged that the remarks objectified women, undermined the dignity of women in public life and lowered the standards of political discourse. The party urged the NCW to examine the video footage of the speech and recommend action for alleged public obscenity and outraging the modesty of women.
Article Summary: Udhayanidhi stalin was arrested from his residence in neelankarai on tuesday. A case was registered against him over his allegedly objectionable remarks made during a rally on the cauvery water dispute in thanjavur. The detention came after he moved the madras high court seeking anticipatory bail, apprehending arrest.

Article Title: Stalker uses husband's name to lure teacher to school gate, stabs her 20 times in Faridabad
Article Text:
Footage shows accused lunge at Sandhya the moment she reaches the classroom entrance, and pull her to the corridor

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think should be done to better prevent stalking-related crimes? GURGAON: A stalker who allegedly pursued a 26-year-old teacher for nearly two years walked into a private school in Faridabad on Monday morning, tricked her into coming to the main gate by using her husband’s name, and then stabbed her more than 20 times in a vicious attack in front of staff and students until the blade bent.Captured on CCTV cameras, the attack unfolded in seconds and left the young English teacher dead before she could be taken to hospital.The accused, Amit (21), a resident of Kot village in Faridabad, was arrested within a couple of hours. Police said he had been stalking Sandhya, who taught at Saraswati Senior Secondary School in Sikrona, and attacked her after she allegedly severed all contact with him and warned him she would approach police if he continued to harass her.Amit entered the school around 9.30am, his face partially covered with a scarf, and asked staff to inform Sandhya that “Vicky” had come to meet her, referring to her husband. Believing her husband was waiting outside, she walked towards the entrance.Footage shows him lunge at Sandhya the moment she reaches the classroom entrance, and pull her to the corridor. Amit punches her as she cries out for help, pulls out a knife in a flash and goes on a stabbing fit, puncturing her neck, abdomen and upper body several times as she slumps to the ground.School principal Tejpal is seen rushing into the corridor to rescue Sandhya after hearing her screams but is forced to step back as the attacker threatens him with the knife.“There were students inside the school and Sandhya was taking classes. He used her husband’s name to call her outside. No sooner did he reach the gate, he attacked her. He stabbed her over 20 times. When I tried to stop him, he threatened to attack me too. We rushed her to Al-Falah Medical College, where she was declared dead on arrival,” the principal told TOI.Police sources said Amit had allegedly bought the knife around two months ago and is suspected to have been planning the murder since then. While the exact number of stab wounds will be confirmed after the autopsy, CCTV footage showed him stabbing Sandhya about 20 times in just 13 seconds. Amit had come to the school on a motorcycle.Sandhya, who had a love marriage with Vikas, is survived by their two children — a five-year-old son and a three-year-old daughter. The attack triggered panic on the campus. Teachers quickly moved frightened children back into classrooms while parents began arriving after news spread. Police cordoned off the school as forensic teams collected evidence.Based on a complaint by Sandhya’s husband, a case was registered under Section 103(1) (murder) of BNS at Sector 58 police station.Police spokesperson Yashpal Yadav said the anti-vehicle theft squad and a team from Sikrona police station tracked down Amit within two hours.“During questioning, the accused said he knew Sandhya from the school in his village where she earlier taught. She later stopped speaking to him and warned of legal action if he continued following her,” Yadav added.Police said the accused will be produced before a local court and his custody sought for further interrogation. CCTV footage and other evidence are being examined as part of the probe, they added.
Article Summary: Footage shows accused lunge at sandhya the moment she reaches the classroom entrance, and pull her to the corridor. Amit (21), a resident of kot village in faridabad, was arrested within a couple of hours. Police said he had been stalking sandhya, who taught at saraswati senior secondary school.

Article Title: In MP village, kids risk lives every day, hop over dam pillars to reach school
Article Text:
Children in Vidisha district risk daily commutes across a river

Poll Vote & Share your view Is the current education system in rural areas, like Kakraua, sufficient to support students? Yes, it meets their needs. No, it needs significant improvement. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





BHOPAL: Children from Kakraua village in MP's Vidisha district are forced to risk their lives every day by negotiating a precarious line of concrete pillars across a check dam on the Betwa river to reach their school - a route they take to avoid a much longer commute.A video of the children hopping perilously across the wide gaps in the check dam has gone viral on social media, raising fresh concerns about local infrastructure and student safety.Kakraua has a school only up to eighth grade.The nearest facility offering education up to 10th grade lies 13km away by road. By crossing the check dam, the distance shrinks to roughly 1.5km, prompting nine students - five of them girls in the ninth grade - to use the risky shortcut daily.The village is part of the constituency of former CM Shivraj Singh Chouhan, who is now the Union minister for agriculture.The dam-crossing involves walking across a series of exposed pillars that stand about three to four feet apart.Students hop about 10 pillars each trip. Villagers say the gap between pillars makes the route hazardous, especially during the monsoon when surfaces become slippery and the river's current increases."We have to work in the fields, so we can't drop our children off at school and back," said a parent."They find it easier to cross the dam nearby... We only have two options: we either stop sending our children to school or continue sending them this way even though it's dangerous."The consequences of skipping the unsafe route are already visible in the community.A student failed her final exams earlier this year after missing school because she could not cross the pillars due to her short height; she is repeating ninth grade this year.Parents fear that continued reliance on the shortcut could lead to further academic setbacks or, worse, an accident.District education officer N K Ahirwar acknowledged the problem. "I visited the spot and informed the collector about this," Ahirwar said."I have written to higher authorities to find a solution soon." However, he did not provide a timeline for the construction of a safe passage for river crossing.Local residents are now pressing authorities for an urgent solution to ensure uninterrupted schooling without endangering children's lives.
Article Summary: Children in vidisha district risk daily commutes across a river to reach their school. A video of the children hopping perilously across the wide gaps in the check dam has gone viral on social media. The village is part of the constituency of former cm shivraj singh chouhan.

Article Title: 'Arrest Abhijeet Dipke immediately': Social media influencer files complaint against CJP founder
Article Text:
Ansari alleged that men associated with Abhijeet Dipke attacked him and urged the police to arrest Dipke immediately.





NEW DELHI: Social media influencer Faizan Ansari on Tuesday said he has filed a written complaint with the Delhi Police against Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke, alleging that men linked to the party attacked him in Maharashtra.Ansari claimed he has evidence to support his allegations and urged the police to arrest Dipke immediately."Today, I have filed a written complaint against Abhijeet Dipke, the founder of the CJP party, with the Delhi DCP, because I have proof that his men attacked me. I was attacked in Pune and in Aurangabad. There are already 2 cases filed on that, " Ansari told ANI.He also praised the Delhi government and police for detaining activist Sonam Wangchuk during the recent protests, claiming the move prevented the law and order situation in the national capital from worsening."I want the Delhi police to immediately arrest Dipke. Moreover, I salute the Delhi CM and the police for detaining Sonam Wangchuk at the right time, due to which the atmosphere in Delhi was saved from deteriorating. Dipke is doing everything for his own benefit, " Ansari added“Moreover, I salute the Delhi CM and the police for detaining Sonam Wangchuk at the right time, due to which the atmosphere in Delhi was saved from deteriorating.Dipke is doing everything for his own benefit,” Ansari alleged.Earlier on Monday, Dipke had rejected comparisons between the CJP-led protests over alleged recruitment and examination irregularities and anti-government movements in Bangladesh and Nepal, saying Indian protesters draw inspiration from Mahatma Gandhi's legacy of peaceful resistance.Dipke also spoke about the CJP's expansion plans, compensation for the families of NEET aspirants who died by suicide, and the state of education in India.Dipke also dismissed exiled Bangladeshi author Taslima Nasreen's remarks comparing the CJP's protest in Delhi against exam irregularities with the 2024 movement that led to the ouster of former Bangladesh prime minister Sheikh Hasina's Awami League government.“Protests in Bangladesh, Nepal are being used to defame us; we are different," he asserted.“We showed during the recent protest in Delhi that we were following the Constitution and holding our demonstration peacefully. Parallels to the protests in Bangladesh and Nepal are being used to defame us.“We don’t need to look at Bangladesh or Nepal when we have Mahatma Gandhi from whom the world takes inspiration to protest,” Dipke said.People are drawing comparisons with the protests in Bangladesh and Nepal because the alleged police brutality reminded them of scenes from those countries, he said.“The students in India were not violent or aggressive. They got their heads, arms and legs broken but displayed restraint and sat peacefully at Jantar Mantar," Dipke said.
Article Summary: Faizan ansari has filed a written complaint with the delhi police against abhijeet dipke. Ansari alleged that men associated with dipke attacked him in maharashtra. He also praised the delhi government and police for detaining activist sonam wangchuk during the recent protests.

Article Title: Bankipur bypoll: Prashant Kishor adds a dash of yellow to Bihar palette of saffron & green
Article Text:
Jan Suraaj party workers celebrating Prashant Kishor's victory





PATNA: Bihar has been green. It has been saffron. Now Prashant Kishor brings yellow.Kishor, architect of poll victories for others, has finally written one for himself, winning his electoral debut in the Bankipur bypoll. It is a signal flare and perhaps a glimpse of a shifting political palette as Jan Suraaj broke through BJP’s saffron and RJD’s green duopoly.Born in Rohtas in 1977, Kishor studied in Buxar, completed his Class XII from Patna Science College, earned a BBA from Lucknow University and a master’s in healthcare management from ASCI, Hyderabad. He did a French language course in France before spending eight years in a UN-supported public health programme.National prominence came after helping design PM Modi’s successful 2014 LS campaign. His organisation, I-PAC, went on to work with multiple political parties. He advised former Bihar CM Nitish Kumar, former Bengal CM Mamata Banerjee and parties across Punjab, Andhra and Tamil Nadu, earning a reputation as one of the country’s most successful political consultants.After helping the Nitish-led Mahagathbandhan win in 2015, Kishor briefly joined JDU before returning to grassroots politics.A self-professed believer in Gandhi’s philosophy, he spent nearly two years on a padayatra across Bihar before launching Jan Suraaj Party on Oct 2, 2024. Its candidates drew a blank in the 2025 state polls, raising questions over whether his campaign skills could translate into votes.Barely eight months later, the answer arrived in Bankipur. Defeat would have dealt a crushing blow to both Kishor and Jan Suraaj. Instead, victory fuelled debate over whether Bihar has room for a third political force.“I did not contest to become an MLA or turn Bankipur into a metropolitan city like Bengaluru,” he said. “I wanted to send a message to BJP brass — generate employment, provide education and stop migration, or be prepared for similar results.”Married to Dr Jahnavi Das and father to a son, Kishor lives like a monk on campaign. He rarely watches TV news, hasn’t used a laptop in a decade, and relies only on his phone to stay connected with his grassroots network.
Article Summary: Prashant kishor has finally written one for himself, winning his electoral debut in the bankipur bypoll. It is a signal flare and perhaps a glimpse of a shifting political palette as jan suraaj broke through bjp’s saffron and rjd's green duopoly.

Article Title: Rahul ignored plan to end my fast, says Sonam Wangchuk
Article Text:
Wangchuk also accused JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh of breaking a promise not to release photos of them offering him soup until he could announce the end of his fast

NEW DELHI: Sonam Wangchuk said his wife Gitanjali had tried to get Rahul Gandhi to offer him juice to end his 26-day hunger strike at Jantar Mantar but received no positive response, leaving him disappointed with the Congress leader and other political parties."We were pondering on breaking my fast through Rahul Gandhi ji and Gitanjali was working on that," Wangchuk told India Today. "She was working hard to see if Rahul ji could break my fast. She didn't get a positive response".Wangchuk also accused Union ministers J P Nadda and Jitendra Singh of breaking a promise not to release photos of them offering him soup until he could announce the end of his fast with opposition and student leaders represented. "They pledged they won't release it and they broke the promise. So I have lost trust in all these leaders," he said.Wangchuk said his wife's subsequent criticism of Rahul had stemmed partly from his own disappointment. He also said netas had come to the Jantar Mantar agitation in small numbers and late. "Similarly, as I said, at Jantar Mantar very few and very late came, so this disappointment caught on her when she made a single comment about them," he added.Gitanjali was targeted online after questioning Rahul's decision to stage a protest outside the PM's residence. Wangchuk said she had made several strong comments against BJP and Hindutva forces as well, but while they kept quiet, the Congress "ecosystem" turned on her for criticising Gandhi."There were four or five very harsh comments about BJP. They didn't react, but the (Congress) ecosystem started trolling her, trolling me," he said. "I am disappointed with the leadership. They shouldn't be so narrow in their approach."Wangchuk, however, was supportive of CJP, whose agitation against examination irregularities he joined at Jantar Mantar. He said he had studied the organisation and found its members "very well-meaning, fair and just and for the right cause, not aligned to any party as such".He welcomed CJP's decision to remain an apolitical pressure group instead of contesting polls. "Being apolitical, it gives voice to the voiceless," he said, adding that this had been his advice to its leadership.
Article Summary: Sonam wangchuk says his wife gitanjali tried to get rahul gandhi to offer him juice to end his 26-day hunger strike at jantar mantar. Wangchuk also accused jp nadda and jitendra singh of breaking a promise not to release photos of them offering him soup until he could announce the end of his fast.

Article Title: Can't exclude SC/ST creamy layer from quotas: Government to Supreme Court
Article Text:
The Centre maintained that altering reservation policies requires empirical research and legislative action.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Opposing the application of the 'creamy layer' criterion for exclusion of affluent members of scheduled caste and scheduled tribe communities from benefits of reservation in jobs and admissions to educational institutions, the government has told the Supreme Court that discrimination against SCs/STs and OBC/SEBC communities do not happen only due to economic considerations."Keeping the broader concept of equality in view, discrimination against SC, ST and OBC/SEBC communities do not happen only based on economic conditions. The system of reservation aims to provide fair opportunities, reduce economic disparities, and foster diversity in governance and academia by addressing historical marginalisation," it said.On Aug 1, 2024, a seven-judge top court verdict permitted states to sub-categorise castes within SC communities based on socio-economic backwardness and the degree of under-representation in government jobs to ensure that the larger pie of 15% quota goes to the most backward. The court had asked governments to devise suitable criteria to bar the 'creamy layer' among the Supreme Court from availing reservation.Filing the affidavit nearly a year after Supreme Court sought response to a PIL by two people - one belonging to SC community and the other to OBC category - on Aug 11 last year, the government said, "Modification of reservation policy, particularly to introduce income-based preferences within reserved categories, should be preceded by a holistic review and thorough empirical study, including socio-economic data of reserved category beneficiaries" and could be done only by Parliament.Parliament alone can modify the list of SC and ST communities entitled to quota, it further stressed.Elaborating upon, it said caste, tribe or part of or group within any caste/tribe can be included or excluded from the list of SCs or STs issued under Articles 341(1) and 342 only by Parliament by law and it is not open to state governments or courts or tribunals or any other authority to modify, amend or alter the list of SCs or STs specified in the notification issued under Clause (1) of Article 341 or 342.Now similar provisions have been made for Socially and Educationally Backward Classes (SEBC) through the Constitution (One Hundred and Second Amendment) Act, 2018, it said.The government said, "In the majority of schemes of welfare and development of SC, ST, and SEBC, excepting reservation in educational institutions and reservation in services under the state, there is a means test which ensures that benefits of schemes percolate to those who actually deserve them."
Article Summary: The centre maintained that altering reservation policies requires empirical research and legislative action. A seven-judge top court verdict permitted states to sub-categorise castes within sc communities. The court had asked governments to devise suitable criteria to bar the 'creamy layer' among the supreme court from availing reservation.

Article Title: 3 rebel TMC MPs to meet Prime Minister today
Article Text:
Three minority breakaway Trinamool Congress MPs will meet PM Modi over breakfast on Friday

KOLKATA/NEW DELHI: Three minority breakaway Trinamool Congress MPs, who are now with the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI) and have so far refused to be a part of the BJP-led NDA, will meet PM Narendra Modi over breakfast on Friday.Murshidabad lawmakers Abu Taher Khan, Khalilur Rahaman and Yusuf Pathan met Union minister Amit Shah on Thursday to voice concerns over SIR tribunals and the removal of loudspeakers from mosques.They have so far stayed away from two NDA meetings. Article Title: Land-grab case: Supeme Court grants interim bail to Abhishek's PA
Article Text:
Abhishek Banerjee's secretary granted a week long interim bail

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday granted a week-long interim bail to Sumit Roy , personal assistant to TMC general secretary Abhishek Banerjee , in the Salboni land-grabbing case but asked him to make himself personally available for investigation in the police station concerned without being accompanied by an advocate or other persons.An FIR was registered against Roy after his name cropped up during the interrogation of former TMC MLA Sujoy Hazra, who was arrested in June. Hazra was accused of selling govt land in Salboni as private land. Roy had allegedly been absconding. The Supreme Court issued notice to the Bengal government on Roy's plea and said, "The petitioner's arrest shall remain stayed till the next date of hearing."

Article Title: BJP to Congress: Let House function, Amit Shah will come
Article Text:
Both Rahul and Kharge have repeatedly questioned Shah’s absence from Parliament, demanding a debate on the Ram temple donation theft

NEW DELHI: The BJP on Thursday accused Congress MPs Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge of deliberately spreading a false narrative of home minister Amit Shah not attending Parliament, saying he cannot be a part of its proceedings when the opposition party will not allow the legislature to function through its unceasing protests.Shah is willing to hear the opposition and will reply emphatically, the BJP said. “Shah is present at his office in the Parliament House all day. But you will not allow Parliament to run... He can attend only when you allow it to function,” BJP MP Ravi Shankar Prasad told reporters in a rejoinder to the LoPs in Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha over their constant attack on Shah over the issue.Both Rahul and Kharge have repeatedly questioned Shah’s absence from Parliament, demanding a debate on the Ram temple donation theft and Shah’s statement on Delhi police’s excesses against student protesters.

Article Title: Rijiju raises point of order, Kharge hits back at minister
Article Text:
Kharge said they had been demanding Shah's statement on police "excess" against students for the past 15 days and that the PM should apologise to students

NEW DELHI: Rajya Sabha on Thursday cleared the Appropriation Bill, 2026, which authorises withdrawal of funds from the Consolidated Fund of India to cover excess expenditure of around Rs 54,067 crore incurred on certain services during the financial year that ended on March 31, 2023. The bill was returned to Lok Sabha after the members' approval through a voice vote - completing the parliamentary process for a Money Bill.During the day, RS saw multiple adjournments, as the opposition members demanded home minister Amit Shah 's presence in the House, leading to RS chairperson C P Radhakrishnan asking parliamentary affairs minister, Kiren Rijiju to convey their sentiments to Shah.In the morning session, the upper House saw two adjournments amid the opposition members also demanding that the chairperson allow the leader of the opposition, Mallikarjun Kharge , to speak. Amid repeated appeals of the chair to the opposition MPs to go back to their seats before he could call LoP, Rijiju raised a point of order. Citing rules, he said Kharge has been saying the same thing every day, and that is a rule against repetition.When the House reconvened at noon, protests continued. Heeding the opposition's request, the chairperson asked Kharge to speak. But the treasury benches objected to this. Amid protests from both sides, Kharge said, "If I don't read the rules, if I don't read my matter, should I read what you (Rijiju) give? It's my right, what to speak, when to speak, how to speak."Kharge said they have been asking PM and Shah to come to the House. "We request the chair to direct the home minister to come and give a statement...," he said. Rijiju objected that Kharge cannot dictate which minister should come on which date. Responding to this, Radhakrishnan said, "No, he (Kharge) is not dictating. He has put his request... As parliamentary affairs minister, you have to reflect the sentiments to HM..."In a press conference, Kharge said they had been demanding Shah's statement on police "excess" against students for the past 15 days and that the PM should apologise to students, but both have been absent from Parliament. "We requested the RS chair that we want the PM's apology and the HM's statement," he said.
Article Summary: The appropriation bill, 2026 authorises withdrawal of funds from the consolidated fund of india to cover excess expenditure of around rs 54,067 crore incurred on certain services during the financial year that ended on march 31, 2023. The bill was returned to lok sabha after the members' approval through a voice vote.

Article Title: Need to seal alliance deal with SP soon for UP polls, MPs tell Congress leadership

NEW DELHI: Congress MPs from Uttar Pradesh have told the party leadership that there should be an alliance with the Samajwadi Party for the 2027 assembly elections, brightening the prospects of a joint challenge to the governing BJP amid continuing pinpricks from local Congress functionaries.Sources said Rahul Gandhi called a meeting with UP Congress MPs on Tuesday, where he sought the views of Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha members on the upcoming assembly polls. Priyanka Gandhi Vadra sat with Rahul during the session.Sources said the MPs expressed a unanimous view that there should be an alliance with SP, and it should be clinched quickly. SP and Congress together bested BJP in UP in the 2024 Lok Sabha polls.However, sources said, the MPs also underlined that the Congress leadership should secure “quality seats” from SP. The stress was as much on winnable seats as on numbers.According to sources, Rahul did not give any idea about the alliance or the tally that the party has in mind for negotiations with SP.The meeting was attended by Pramod Tiwari, Rajiv Shukla, Imran Pratapgarhi, Kishori Lal Sharma, Ujjwal Raman Singh, Rajesh Rathore, Tanuj Punia and Imran Masood.Sources said one MP cited the example of Bihar elections in 2015 and 2021 to illustrate how the party should focus on winnable seats. While Congress secured fewer seats in 2015 but scored a high tally, its score fell sharply despite contesting a high number five years later.Many participants felt the mood of the meeting suggested that an alliance with SP would be finalised soon, and seat-sharing talks would start in earnest. It is said that the newly-appointed UP Congress in-charge, Rajendra Pal Gautam, has undertaken an exercise on seats, while the party has also ordered a survey to assess its strength in individual constituencies.In the INDIA bloc meeting in June, SP chief Akhilesh Yadav had asked Congress to show a “large heart” and trust the judgement of the regional parties in states.
Article Summary: Sources said rahul gandhi called a meeting with up congress mps on tuesday. He sought the views of rajya sabha and lok sabha members on the upcoming assembly polls. Article Title: Supreme Court dismisses plea challenging Delhi HC relief to Hinduja brothers in Bofors case
Article Text:
The case stems from the Bofors scandal involving the Rs 1,437 crore howitzer gun deal signed between India and Swedish arms manufacturer Bofors in 1986

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday dismissed a plea challenging the Delhi high court’s 2005 decision that had quashed criminal proceedings against the Hinduja brothers in the Bofors payoff case, effectively bringing an end to the long-pending appeal filed by advocate Ajay K Agrawal.A bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and Vinod K Chandran refused to adjourn the matter and declined to entertain further submissions during the hearing.The petitioner, appearing virtually, sought four weeks’ time to delete the names of respondents who had died. “I’m seeking four weeks’ time for deletion of the names, as respondent nos. 1 and 4 have expired,” the advocate told the court.Justice Pardiwala questioned the continued pendency of the matter and remarked, “What is all this about the Hinduja brothers and the CBI?”When informed that the Delhi high court had exonerated the accused and quashed the proceedings, Justice Pardiwala said, “All proceedings were quashed. What is this? How many years have passed?”The petitioner responded that “The deal occurred in 1986.”As another counsel attempted to make submissions, Justice Pardiwala made it clear that the court would not postpone the matter. “No question of adjournment. It is a 2018 matter,” he said.Counsel appearing in the case argued that a separate appeal filed by the Central Bureau of Investigation had earlier been dismissed by the Supreme Court on the ground that the agency was already a respondent in the present petition and could raise all its arguments here.The case stems from the Bofors scandal involving the Rs 1,437 crore howitzer gun deal signed between India and Swedish arms manufacturer Bofors in 1986. The CBI had alleged that the Hinduja brothers received millions in illegal payoffs linked to the contract.According to the investigation, Bofors paid nearly Rs 64 crore in kickbacks, with secret Swiss bank code names including Lotus and Tulip allegedly linked to the Hinduja family. The Delhi high court, however, quashed the criminal proceedings against the brothers in 2005, a decision that remained under challenge until the Supreme Court dismissed the appeal on Friday.
Article Summary: The supreme court dismissed a plea challenging the delhi high court’s 2005 decision that had quashed criminal proceedings against the hinduja brothers in the bofors payoff case. A bench of justices jb pardiwala and vinod k chandran refused to adjourn the matter and declined to entertain further submissions.

Article Title: Weeding out dead wood aim of compulsory retirement, says Supreme Court
Article Text:
The SC said that compulsory retirement is open to judicial scrutiny if the order is mala fide, arbitrary or perverse

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: It is not punitive to hand out compulsory retirement to someone, particularly in the armed forces, whose performance is slackening over the years, the Supreme Court said Thursday while rejecting the plea of a CISF officer challenging his removal from service on the ground of poor performance.A bench of Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and Shree Chandrashekhar said compulsory retirement should not be seen as punitive but as a measure needed to ensure a high standard of efficiency and discipline in the force. "The object underlying compulsory retirement is to weed out the dead wood so as to maintain a high standard of efficiency and integrity in public service," the bench said, adding such an order is "not punitive in nature", carries no stigma and is passed in public interest on the government's subjective satisfaction.It, however, said compulsory retirement is open to judicial scrutiny if the order is mala fide, arbitrary or perverse.Rejecting the officer's plea, the bench noted his performance had declined in the two years preceding the retirement order, with gradings dropping from "Good" to "Average". Members of disciplined forces are expected to maintain consistently high standards of efficiency, vigilance and discipline, it said.
Article Summary: Supreme court rejects plea of a cisf officer challenging his removal from service on the ground of poor performance. Justices prashant kumar mishra and shree chandrashekhar said compulsory retirement should not be seen as punitive. Members of disciplined forces are expected to maintain consistently high standards of efficiency, vigilance and discipline, it said.
